playbook:
When I see two others pledge scout and I can actually afford a raid after paying my pledge cost, I pledge raid to exploit their passivity and steal points — but only if I will be the lone raider and the clockwise target has not pledged escort.

Always remember pledge costs are deducted immediately; I must check my fuel balance at pledge time and only pledge actions whose cost I can pay then. Do not pledge raid or escort if I cannot pay the pledge cost immediately.

Never submit an act that contradicts my recorded pledge. My act must repeat my recorded pledge word-for-word; plan my pledge to match the action I will perform at the act stage.

At act time, re-check recorded pledge and remaining fuel (after pledge deduction). If my recorded pledge is unaffordable given current bookkeeping (it should not be if I followed the pledge-time check), correct future behavior so this never happens. If in doubt about legality or affordability at act time, default to scout only if my recorded pledge was scout; otherwise accept that I must not have pledged the unaffordable action in the first place.

If I pledge escort, I must intend to escort (and have paid the escort cost). Use escort when I want to protect myself from incoming theft (it prevents raids from my left/West) or when I want a guaranteed 2 POINTS while conserving fuel relative to raiding.

If I pledge scout, I must intend to scout. Scout is the lowest-cost safe option when my fuel is low, when I need to avoid overspending or illegal acts, or when conserving fuel for endgame leftover-point value.

When I am the lone raider and both my clockwise target and the other neighbor are scouting, raid is high-value: it transfers 3 points from my clockwise target unless that target escorted. Prefer raid in that scenario when it is affordable and I will remain legal after pledge deduction.

Do not raid when my clockwise target has pledged escort — an escort prevents theft and a raid against an escort costs me 1 POINT with no gain. Avoid wasting fuel and points on such raids.

When both opponents consistently scout, alternate between raiding (to punish passivity and gain points) and scouting (to conserve fuel) based on fuel level: prefer raid when I need points and have a fuel margin, prefer scout when fuel is getting low or when the pledge-stage bookkeeping would leave me unable to pay later costs.

When I am ahead with moderate fuel, prefer escort to protect the lead and conserve fuel for final rounds rather than risking expensive raids that might backfire or leave me unable to act legally later.

When I am behind late in the match and can afford raids, prioritize raids to try to close the gap, accepting higher risk if necessary to change standings — but still ensure I can pay the pledge cost immediately.

If a round’s pledges put me in the minority (e.g., I’m the only escort or the only raid), choose the pledge consistent with both my fuel and scoring needs: join the defensive posture if I need stability, or raid only if the cost is justified and affordable given pledge-time deduction and act-time intent.

Keep an explicit running check of fuel after paying my pledge cost and before the act stage; do not let fuel go negative. If my bookkeeping would result in negative fuel, change my pledge choices earlier — do not try to act raid/escort if my recorded pledge and fuel don’t permit it.

Value leftover fuel as 1 point each in final scoring; when scores are close near the end, weigh conserving fuel against risking raids that could flip the standings and remember leftover fuel can decide ties.

When opponents show patterns (consistent scouting, occasional escorts, or starting to raid back), adapt: exploit predictable scouting with raids when affordable, switch to escorts if I need protection from incoming raids (especially from my left), and switch to scouting to rebuild fuel when opponents become unpredictable.

If I ever doubt the state of fuel, the legality of a pledge, or whether my recorded pledge will be affordable at act time, prefer conservative choices at pledge time (scout or escort I can pay) rather than over-committing to raids that I cannot legally perform.

Explicit operational checklist before submitting a pledge:
- Compute current fuel minus the pledge cost; if negative, do not choose that pledge.
- Consider opponents’ visible pledges to decide whether a raid would be effective (target must be scout, not escort).
- Ensure my intended act equals my pledge.
- If I intend to preserve fuel for endgame points, prefer scout/escort accordingly.

I revise nothing else from my prior playbook except to tighten enforcement of the pledge-time affordability check and the invariant that act must equal recorded pledge; these are non-negotiable constraints that prevent illegal acts and negative fuel.
